hourly.summary: United fans are in that familiar 'new manager, same old chaos' limbo — venting about Wilcox, listing a terrifyingly long to-do list for Pochettino ("reanimate the corpse of Sesko" is peak gallows humour), and side-eyeing Dalot and Mount. There's a flicker of curiosity about Poch's first moves, but mostly it's the weary resignation of supporters who've seen this movie before and know the script by heart.

daily.summary: Fan sentiment deteriorated sharply from morning cynicism to afternoon fury, as a leaked zebra-striped kit design ignited fresh outrage atop existing transfer frustrations and ownership anger. Nostalgic reflections on Rooney's debut gave way to grim amusement over Pochettino links and sobering concern for the club legend's mental health struggles. The day's trajectory reflects a fanbase moving from resigned sarcasm to active revolt against the club's direction.

weekly.summary: Fan sentiment began in existential crisis (2/10) with the club in the relegation zone and ownership rage dominant, briefly lifted by Pochettino rumors (4/10) before crashing again on Carrick's sacking (2/10). His appointment brought apprehensive hope (4-5/10) that quickly faded into disillusionment (3/10), finally settling into a dark, resigned acceptance of mediocrity (5/10) laced with gallows humor. The week traces an arc from acute despair through false dawns to cynical resignation, with structural anger at the Glazers/INEOS ownership remaining the constant undercurrent.
